notes: Derived edit (scouting 0004, fixed per the review). Derivability likely: the class-level fact is not stated in any exact form tried, while both premises are. Worlds: w1, ticks become insects (with what goes with that); w2, Lyme gets an insect carrier. 'Ticks are arachnids' is entangled with firm facts (eight legs, related to spiders), so a strict reviewer could drop w1; it is kept because the README lets a premise give way together with its side facts. No exception world: the premise is a membership, not a property rule, and 'deer ticks' in the premise query closes the sub-case 'only Lyme ticks are insects'. The scouting's leg-count premise-route query was replaced (fleas or ticks' leg counts are separate firm facts and would split w1); the premise route asks the carrier's class through its description, and the class comparison uses mosquitoes. R4/R1 risk: loose web text calls Lyme 'insect-borne' (1,305 co-occurrences, about 10x the explicit arachnid statements), so some models may answer insect before the edit; the prompts name biological classes explicitly so that the colloquial 'bug' sense is excluded. Verifier: the R4 risk is kept as a measured risk, not a disqualifier: the direct prompt asks for the biological class explicitly, so a model that knows ticks are arachnids should answer arachnid before the edit, and the model audit drops the record for any model that does not. Formal check (FINDINGS B3): the 'insect or arachnid?' questions take for granted that Lyme disease has carriers of one class and that no animal is both; transmitted_by_class is many-valued in general (some diseases have vectors of both classes), so both are stated per record as bridges with checks. q3 asked about 'deer ticks', which the chains read as the premise's ticks; it now asks about ticks. Since 2026-10-31 the questions say 'arthropods', not 'animals', and so does the one-class bridge, as in biology-replace-0003: deer and mice are also said to spread Lyme disease; its arthropod vectors are ticks only.
